notes.text:
The collection has a generic BM `rei-miro-britanico` record, but its supporting source gives no distinguishing description or accession. Several BM rei miro records in this batch could fit it. The catalogue labels this combined field “Found/Acquired”; it is retained as source wording and is not treated as an independently established findspot. A separate “Production place” field is represented as made_at when present.

30 September 2026 identity review: ambiguous crosswalk to `rei-miro-britanico`; keep this catalogue source unlinked. The British Museum identifies Museum number Oc.6330, CDMS Oc1870C1.6330 and miscellaneous number Oc1870C0504.5 (https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/E_Oc-6330_1). Its 1870 Christy register describes a thin light-brown crescent with heads, perforated ears, a grooved upper edge and hollowed back; one head was broken and refastened. It measures 38 × 67.5 × 4.5 cm. Lt M.J. Harrison presented it on 4 May 1870 and recorded obtaining it on Easter Island in 1868 during HMS Topaze's cruise; the BM cites supplementary Christy Register folio 132 and Dalton's 1904 photograph. The generic Arte row gives only type and holder. Resolution needs a description, image or accession crosswalk for that specific row; the Dalton citation alone does not establish the connection.
